journal: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
title: A Fast Threshold Neural Network for Ship Detection in Large-Scene SAR Images
categories: Journal: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
summary: Multiscale ship detection in large-scene offshore synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images is of great significance in civil and military fields, such as maritime management and wartime reconnaissance. Methods based on deep learning apply a deep neural network to extract multiscale information from SAR images, which improves detection performance. However, deep neural networks are computationally complex, and even with GPU acceleration, the timeliness of ship detection in large-scene SAR images is still constrained. Methods based on threshold segmentation, in contrast, are efficient and straightforward, but they are less robust and need to be adjusted with complex and changing scenes. This article combines two methods and proposes a lightweight framework based on a threshold neural network (TNN) to achieve fast detection. Specifically, the TNN is carefully designed to extract the grayscale features of the SAR image, which predicts the optimal detection threshold within the sliding window and separates the targets adaptively. In addition, a false alarm rejection network is used to discriminate candidate targets and improve detection accuracy. Experiments are carried out on the public SSDD offshore dataset and the FUSAR-Ship-Detection dataset. The results show that the proposed framework performs 14.43% better than the Multi-CFAR for the SSDD offshore dataset and 7.36% better for the FUSAR-Ship-Detection dataset when using F1 as the metric. Furthermore, the floating point operations of the proposed framework are only 1/240 of those of YOLO-v4 with comparable performance.

journal: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
title: PolSAR Ship Detection Based on Superpixel-Level Contrast Enhancement
categories: Journal: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
summary: Ship detection in polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) images has attracted widespread attention in recent years. However, pixel level detection methods are heavily affected by inherent speckle noise. In this letter, we proposed a detection method that enhances the ship-sea contrast beforehand by combining local statistical saliency and scattering mechanism coherence in superpixel-level. Firstly, simple linear iterative clustering (SLIC) based segmentation method is adopted for PolSAR images to generate superpixels. Then, local saliency is calculated based on superpixel-level similarity from the perspective of statistical characteristics. Based on this, the superpixel-level modified polarimetric coherence metric is obtained from the perspective of physical scattering mechanisms, which can help distinguish small ships with low saliency and strong sea clutters with high saliency. Ship detection is achieved by combining the two features above. The experimental results based on real PolSAR data show that compared with other classic and state-of-the-art methods, the proposed method has improved the figure of merit by at least 4.28% and has increased the target clutter ratio by at least 8.43 decibel (dB) on average.

AI.tldr: A hand-crafted superpixel-level contrast-enhancement method for PolSAR ship detection that fuses local statistical saliency with a modified polarimetric coherence metric, reporting FoM and TCR gains on real PolSAR data.
AI.research_relevance: Relevant to remote-sensing ship detection in PolSAR imagery and to speckle-robust preprocessing, but it is a classical hand-crafted method with no learning-based detector and no lightweighting or deployment component. Relevance to onboard model lightweighting is therefore indirect and limited.
AI.task_and_scene: Ship detection in polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) images, maritime scene. Target class: ships (including small ships with low saliency). Modality: PolSAR.
AI.model_architecture: Not a deep model. Pipeline: (1) SLIC-based superpixel segmentation of PolSAR images; (2) superpixel-level local statistical saliency from similarity; (3) superpixel-level modified polarimetric coherence metric from physical scattering mechanisms; (4) fusion of the two features for ship detection. No neural network architecture is described.
AI.lightweight_method: None. The method is a hand-crafted, non-learning preprocessing/feature-fusion approach (SLIC superpixel segmentation, statistical saliency, and polarimetric coherence). No pruning, quantization, distillation, NAS, or lightweight network design is involved.
AI.onboard_deployability: No deployment evidence. Abstract does not report parameters, FLOPs, latency, memory, energy, or any edge/onboard hardware. The superpixel segmentation step (SLIC) is typically compute-intensive, but its cost is not quantified here.
AI.datasets_and_metrics: Real PolSAR data (specific sensor/dataset not named in abstract). Metrics: figure of merit (FoM) and target-to-clutter ratio (TCR, in dB). Abstract reports FoM improvement of at least 4.28% and average TCR increase of at least 8.43 dB versus classic and state-of-the-art methods.
AI.experiments: Comparison against classic and state-of-the-art ship detection methods on real PolSAR data. Reported gains: FoM improved by at least 4.28%; TCR increased by at least 8.43 dB on average. No ablation details, no per-dataset breakdown, and no computational cost comparison are given in the abstract.
AI.limitations: Abstract does not specify the PolSAR sensor/dataset, image size, number of test scenes, or the exact baseline methods. No computational cost (runtime, memory), parameter count, or hardware/deployment evidence is reported. The method is not learning-based and is not evaluated for onboard or real-time use; speckle robustness is addressed only at the superpixel level.
AI.ideas_for_my_research: The superpixel-level contrast-enhancement idea (SLIC segmentation + local statistical saliency + modified polarimetric coherence) is a preprocessing pipeline that could be reused as a front-end for a lightweight detector to suppress speckle before a small CNN head, potentially reducing the network's burden on speckle-robust feature learning. However, the method is hand-crafted and not integrated with any learning-based detector, so the transferable value is limited to a preprocessing module; no evidence of its cost (superpixel segmentation latency) or compatibility with onboard constraints is provided.

journal: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
title: Small Ship Detection of SAR Images Based on Optimized Feature Pyramid and Sample Augmentation
categories: Journal: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
summary: SAR images have become the latest high-resolution imaging equipment, which can monitor the Earth 24 hours a day. More and more deep learning technologies are applied to ship target detection, however, in complex environments, due to the small target of the ship, problems such as false detection and miss detection often occur. For this reason, SSPNet is proposed with several small-target-augmentation strategies to complete the detection of small ships on the sea. This network is an improvement of FPN. The model uses Context Attention Module (CAM), Scale Enhancement Module (SEM), and Scale Selection Module (SSM). CAM introduces the attention heat map, SEM uses the residual module to make the network pay more attention to specific scale targets, SSM introduces deep semantic features into shallow features. Weighted Negative Sampling (WNS) strategy is proposed to enable the network to select more representative samples. These modules make the network more suitable for small target detection. The results on SSDD dataset show that the model is superior to the existing object detection network, and the AP50 reaches 91.57%.

journal: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
title: Toward Accurate Infrared Small Target Detection via Edge-Aware Gated Transformer
categories: Journal: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
summary: Extracting small targets from complex backgrounds is the eventual goal of single infrared small target detection (SISTD), which has many potential applications in defense security and marine rescue. Recently, methods utilizing deep learning have shown their superiority over traditional theoretical approaches. However, they do not consider both the global semantics and specific shape information, thereby limiting their performance. To overcome this proplem, we propose a Gated Shaped TransUnet (GSTUnet), designed to fully utilize shape information while detecting small target detection. Specifically, we have proposed a multi-scale encoder branch to extract global features of small targets at different scales. Then, the extracted global features are passed through a gated -shaped stream branch that focuses on the shape information of small targets through gate convolutions. Finally, we fuse there features to obtain the final result. Our GSTUnet learns both global and shape information through the aforementioned two branches, establishing global relationships between different feature scales. The GSTUnet demonstrates excellent evaluation metrics on various datasets, outperforming current state-of-the-art methods. To access our code and datasets, please visit the following link:https://github.com

AI.ideas_for_my_research: 1) The gated-shape stream branch (gate convolutions) is a transferable idea for small-target detection: shape/edge priors can be injected into a lightweight detector to compensate for the weak appearance of small targets. 2) The multi-scale encoder branch could be replaced by a lightweight backbone (e.g., MobileNet/ShuffleNet-style) to test accuracy-vs-parameter trade-offs for onboard use. 3) The gated fusion of global and shape streams is a candidate module to distill into a compact student network via knowledge distillation. 4) Since the paper targets infrared small targets (defense/marine rescue), its shape-gating mechanism may transfer to ship/vehicle detection in satellite imagery where targets are also small and low-contrast.
